tokyo_daikokuya_tempura.price_note: Full menu with prices from the shop’s own おしながき page; the site states 消費税は表示価格に含まれております, tax included. Tabelog not consulted: it has served Cf-Mitigated: challenge (HTTP 403) to this egress since 2026-09-02. ⚠ THIS IS A TEMPURA HOUSE AND THERE IS NOTHING HERE FOR A COELIAC ON THE MAIN BOARD — every tendon and every tempura plate is wheat batter, and the tare poured over a Daikokuya tendon is soy, mirin and sugar. That is said plainly rather than worked around. ⚠ WHAT IS WORTH RECORDING IS THE SIDE BOARD, because an old Asakusa tempura shop keeps a proper 一品 list and several of those plates have no flour in them at all: さしみ ¥2,400, あじのたたき ¥900, 胡瓜もみ ¥700, おろし和え ¥700 and なめたけおろし和え ¥500 are constructed without batter. All are eaten with soy sauce, which is where the wheat sits, and all but the cucumber are fish. 茄子のしぎやき at ¥800 is aubergine in miso — the one plate here that is plant in substance. ⚠ AND ONE PORTION NOTE THAT MATTERS FOR A GROUP: 御飯 is ¥250 and お吸物 ¥350, so a person who cannot eat tempura can sit down to rice, soup and pickles for well under ¥1,000 while the table has tendon. The soup is a dashi, so it is bonito.

Raw fish, and the most expensive side plate. No wheat in the fish — the soy sauce is the wheat, so bring tamari.

items.en: Nuta — seafood and spring onion in vinegared miso
items.note: Dressed in 酢味噌, vinegared MISO, whose koji is sometimes barley. Normally contains fish or shellfish.
Raw fish chopped with spring onion and ginger — no batter, and eaten with soy.
A 酢の物 dressing is 三杯酢 — vinegar, sugar and SOY, usually with dashi.
Egg. A tempura shop’s tamagoyaki is normally made with dashi, which would make it fish as well.
⚠ THE ONE PLATE HERE THAT IS PLANT IN SUBSTANCE: aubergine fried and spread with miso. The miso is the gluten-or-barley question, and shigiyaki miso often carries mirin and dashi.
Cucumber salted and squeezed — about as short an ingredient list as a Japanese side gets, and plant. The dressing is normally a vinegar one, occasionally with soy.
Jellyfish is animal; the dressing is soy-based.
Grated daikon — plant — dressed, and a Japanese 和え dressing is soy and often dashi.
⚠ Kamaboko is a steamed FISH CAKE routinely bulked with WHEAT STARCH — a quiet wheat item that reads as plain fish.
Enoki mushrooms and daikon, both plant — but なめたけ in Japan usually means the bottled enoki preserve simmered in SOY SAUCE and mirin, which is the wheat.
Sake is rice, water and koji; the coeliac caveat is only that koji is occasionally grown on barley.
